chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, a servant may be oppressed, so he continues to supplicate (or curse) until he becomes the oppressor.

key_terms.یَدْعُو: supplicates / calls out (often implies cursing in this context)

ai.seo_question: How does continuous supplication or cursing affect an oppressed person's status?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates how prolonged endurance of injustice, coupled with persistent supplication or cursing, can gradually erode one's spiritual equilibrium, leading to a transformation from the oppressed to the oppressor. This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, underscores the psychological and spiritual volatility of the believer under duress, serving as a cautionary note on the dangers of letting grievance consume one's character. It highlights the delicate balance between patience (sabr) and the potential for spiritual degradation if the heart becomes hardened by perceived injustice.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: It   is   narrated   that   Imam   Ja’far   Sadiq   (a.s.)   said, “Sometimes a person is a victim of oppression and he curses till the time he himself becomes the oppressor.”
